Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard hatchling.build backend. No evidence of setup.py, custom PEP 517 hooks, .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py install/startup execution was identified.
  • src/pyfies/__init__.py only imports package symbols and defines __version__; there is no import-time network, file harvesting, or process execution evidence.
  • The user-run script scripts/generate_r_fixtures.R appears to generate R parity fixtures and is not an automatic execution path during package installation or Python interpreter startup.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no broad collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallets, or kubeconfig was identified.
  • Staging/exfiltration: no archive staging followed by upload, webhook use, raw IP endpoint, or paste/drop-service transfer was identified.
  • Persistence: no cron, systemd, launch agent, shell profile modification, background polling loop, or similar persistence mechanism was identified.
  • Lateral movement: no Kubernetes service-account use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection evidence was identified.
  • Obfuscation/loader behavior: no eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal loader, downloader stub, or obfuscated payload was identified.
  • The pre-scan match on suppressPackageStartupMessages is an R package startup-message suppression construct and does not plausibly indicate persistence.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Hidden paths such as .github/workflows, .gitignore, and .pre-commit-config.yaml are present in the sdist, but these are common development/CI files in source distributions; no malicious execution or token-theft logic was found in them.
  • Dependencies appear to be numpy, scipy, pandas, plus development/documentation optional dependencies; no suspicious sudden dependency insertion or typosquatting evidence was identified.
  • No unexplained native binaries, hidden payloads, or wheel/sdist mismatch evidence was visible in the provided extracted text.
